originality.rationale: The full source arXiv:2610.13846v1 proves one-anchor bounds and explicitly notes the nontrivial multi-anchor problem in Section 7. The present exact simultaneous boundary interval and three-anchor pairwise/nonjoint compatibility family are not statements or immediate consequences of its one-anchor pointwise sharpness; its separate extremizers cannot be naively combined. Fuchs arXiv:2112.10147 develops the transformation but no matching compatibility theorem. Targeted searches and primary comparisons found no statement logically covering these results; possible implicit multithreshold literature remains a qualified risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent multithreshold feasibility result may be implicit in completely positive matrix or conditional-moment literature not captured by the searches.
The theorem applies to a saturated and minimum-second-moment boundary slice, not arbitrary prescribed anchors.

value.rationale: The motivating primary paper explicitly isolates multi-anchor feasibility as nontrivial. The new exact sharp interval resolves a mathematically natural simultaneous two-anchor boundary slice and yields a continuum of genuine pairwise feasibility without global feasibility. This has intrinsic relevance for copula-based inference and inverse dependence specification rather than being a routine numerical special case.
